description: No clean concept found. Activation is a board-state function seen from the player to move, mostly mid-game, loosely tied to stones in the lower centre-right and column 0: opponent stones at (1,0),(2,0) and (0,3), mine at (1,3) and (2,4), opponent at (1,4). These cells raise it on average, but stones elsewhere can switch it on or off, so no simple rule predicts firing well.
effect: None measurable: forcing it to zero or to max changes move probabilities by at most about 0.05 on any column (8 positions).
notes: 6 dev calls. Best was a hand-weighted cell sum with weights read off firing-vs-nonfiring cell counts, threshold 8: F1 0.167 (P 0.13, R 0.22), AUROC 0.59, sim share 0.28. Cell-pair conjunctions scored F1 0.13-0.14, 'non-immediate threat' 0.07, and open diagonal lines 0.11. Minimal pairs showed strong non-additive context effects, e.g. one far-away stone pair kills a firing checkerboard pattern. It may be a random direction or a mixture. Two synthesis positions beat the dev max (4.53, 4.49).
